fields.title: 1. T5 — Confirmation Terms of the $40 Billion Financing (8-K): Observation Results
fields.md:
| Item | October issue (2026-10-23 AM) record | Confirmed this round | Source grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8-K filed | Not disclosed | **Not disclosed** — the latest filings for CIK 1181412 are the S-8 and 10-Q of 2026-10-22; the last 8-K is the 10/20 earnings release | ① [EDGAR filing list](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001181412&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=25), accessed 2026-10-23 |
| 10-Q subsequent events | — | The debt note (R65) contains **no** mention of new financing after 2026-09-30 — it lists only corporate bonds of $25 billion (5 tranches, weighted average 5.855%, effective 6.072%, coupon rates 5.35–6.65%), an undrawn $5 billion revolver, and 3 failed sale-leasebacks totaling $12,897M | ① [10-Q R65](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R65.htm), 2026-10-22 |
| Size · arrangers | $40 billion, arranged by Apollo | $40 billion, **jointly arranged by Apollo and Goldman Sachs** (both declined to comment) | ⑤ [Semafor 10/22](https://www.semafor.com/article/10/22/2026/spacex-40b-debt-deal-will-cost-it-as-ai-fears-spread) |
| Interest rate (reported) | Secured about 7.75% · lowest tranche about 8.3% | No change — lowest tranche about 8.3%, chip-secured tranche about 7.75% (more than 1%p above the trading yield of existing bonds) | ⑤ Same as above |
| Pricing timing | Targeting 2027 close | Expected to be finalized **"next week" (week of 10/26)**; may change before finalization | ⑤ Same as above |
| Collateral · maturity · equity components | Some GPUs as collateral (reported) | Only collateral = "some of the company's chips" is confirmed. **Tranche sizes, maturities, conversion and equity-raise components appear in no report** | ⑤ Same as above |
| Conflicting report | — | "SpaceX prices $8.3 billion debt deal" (10/22) — the body says "finalizing"; the amount does not appear in the body and its digits coincide with the 8.3% rate; no source cited → **not adopted** | Unrated [Gokhshtein](https://gokhshtein.com/news/2026-10-22-spacex-prices-83b-debt-deal-as-apollo-goldman-lead) |

**Verdict**: T5 has **not occurred**. Milestone D-2027-1 ("2027 additional financing of $50 billion or less AND no equity raise") remains `Undetermined`, as the determination year has not arrived and there is no filing. Proposed new rule ② (a 5%p bearish adjustment if a rate above 8% is finalized) can be deliberated only if an 8-K exists — the reported 8.3% is not a subject for deliberation (source: `state.rule_proposals_not_applied`).

**Two attribution corrections to the October issue** — this round we reopened the original Semafor 10/07 article ([Semafor 10/07](https://www.semafor.com/article/10/07/2026/spacex-looks-to-40-billion-debt-raise-to-buy-chips)). What is actually in that article: $40 billion (citing the FT), use of proceeds Nvidia chips, Apollo as a "possible lender", credit rating BBB (2 notches below Meta and Alphabet), and debt relative to earnings about 5 times Alphabet's and about 3 times Meta's. **What is not there**: ① the split of "about $10 billion in bank loans + about $30 billion in IG bonds" ② "5-year CDS 197.6bp, a record high". The October issue attributed both to that article — the split appears to come from secondary reports (reprinting FT and Bloomberg), and the original source of the CDS figure was not found this round. These two numbers are **downgraded to 'source unconfirmed'** and recorded in the state's T5 notes and open_questions. The CDS mention in the 10/22 article is only the statement that "default insurance has widened", with no figure.

**Comparison baseline confirmed by the 10-Q** (source: [10-Q R65](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R65.htm)): the reported rates of 7.75–8.3% are +190–245bp above the June corporate bond weighted average of 5.855% (calculation: 7.75 − 5.855 = 1.895 / 8.3 − 5.855 = 2.445), and lower than the 12.5% secured notes and the 9.5% B-3 term loan that xAI priced in 2025. That is, the framing of "replacing xAI's debt with SpaceX's credit" remains valid, but the key point of the reports is that pricing has not returned to June levels.
